correctness.rationale: Given source recovery lifetimes, receiver states solve q′=h(1-q)-mu q independently. Linearization q0=(lambda/m)exp(-mu t)sum_i int_0^(L_i wedge t)exp(mu s)ds has n E q0->lambda Phi(theta)exp(-x) at t=log n+loglog n+x, and variance O(1/log n) from independent source lifetimes. The difference q0-q is nonnegative and has expectation at scale n bounded O(1/log n) via the explicit two-source covariance. Conditional binomial n,q then converges to Poisson; surviving source probability ≤m exp(-t)=O(1/log n), and zero infected is absorbing, giving the Gumbel zero-atom. The detuning theta=0 follows from continuous exponential quotient. Independent finite formula computations support normalization, albeit slow convergence at finite n when theta<0.
